Hi Connor —

We started seeing intermittent generation failures and a spike in tail latency on our dedicated cluster around 08:55 PT. The requests are returning a mix of 503s and "generation failed: kv-cache not found" errors for a subset of warm nodes. This is impacting our user-facing service (batch + streaming) — roughly 8% of calls in the last 20 minutes.

Attached is a short sample of the failure log from one of our client threads (error-sample.log.txt). Can you confirm whether this looks like a Redwood-side allocator or KV cache problem?

We need an ETA on mitigation; if this persists we'll have to pause a production rollout tonight.

Thanks,
Maya Fernandez

Hi Maya — thanks for the quick note and the log excerpt. We've opened a high-priority investigation. Initial triage notes:

- Behavior looks consistent with intermittent KV cache misses on a subset of warm nodes — the allocator may have rebalanced work in a way that caused fragmentary warm-connections and increased cache miss rates.
- I'm spinning up an ops incident and will get on a short technical sync with eng.

Immediate asks for you:
1) If you can, please share a short Trace ID or two from failed requests (the ones in the sample look like trace: 6c3f-7a2b-21).
2) Confirm if you have any pinned model variants for this pool.

Short-term mitigation we plan to try in the next 30–90 minutes: pin the traffic from your tenant to the current warm-subset and increase warmup concurrency so nodes aren't evicted mid-request. We'll also pull allocator logs and compare session affinity.

I will follow up with a concrete rollback/patch plan and a remediation checklist.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-12T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Generation failures and high tail latency in Cerebra Labs — triage notes

Karthik / Jordan — forwarding Maya's report and my initial ack. Early engineering read: allocator's regional balancing made an aggressive compaction pass during a low-traffic interval; that compaction temporarily fragmented warm-state so a subset of sessions landed on nodes with stale/empty KV caches. Symptoms: elevated token retransmits and 5xx errors for in-flight streaming connections.

Proposed immediate mitigations (we can implement as hotfix via config change):
- Action A: Bind Cerebra tenant to existing warm-node set for 60 minutes (prevents rebalance while we stabilize).
- Action B: Increase warmup_concurrency from 4 -> 12 for the affected pool to speed KV population.
- Action C: Apply a short TTL extension for KV entries (increase from 2m -> 6m) to reduce cold misses during rolling operations.

I'll stage these behind a canary and watch realtime QPS/latency. If accepted, I can push the patch and coordinate with Support to update the customer. Attached is a small config diff and a remediation checklist: allocator-config-diff.patch (link: https://drive.redwood/example/allocator-config-diff.patch) and remediation-checklist.pdf.

Notes and concerns: we should monitor for CPU/VRAM pressure with higher warmup concurrency — Jordan, can you run a quick capacity check for the US-west pool?

Connor

(attachment: allocator-config-diff.patch, remediation-checklist.pdf)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-13T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected node fragmentation causing token errors — remediation timeline

Hi Maya — quick update and the actions we've taken: 

What we observed: allocator rebalance during a compaction window temporarily fragmented warm node membership for your tenant which caused intermittent KV cache misses and elevated tail latency for in-flight streaming calls.

What we did (completed 08:10 PT):
- Pinned traffic for Cerebra Labs to the currently warmed node set (60-minute binding).
- Increased warmup_concurrency from 4 to 12 for your dedicated pool.
- Extended KV TTL from 2m to 6m for the affected node set.

Immediate impact: error rate dropped from ~8% to ~0.8% within 10 minutes of the change; tail latency decayed to baseline within ~18 minutes. We'll keep the binding in place until midnight PT and then transition to a graceful rebalance with controlled warmup thresholds.

Next steps / deliverables:
- Tonight (by 23:00 PT): controlled rebalance with staged warmup (we will run a canary, watch metrics, and rollback if violations occur).
- By 2026-10-14 EOD: post-incident summary and root cause analysis (RCA) with concrete remediation to allocator heuristics.
- Compensation: we'll propose a partial SLA credit for the impacted window; Hannah will follow up with the credit proposal and scope.

Attachments: allocator-config-diff.patch, remediation-checklist.pdf, excerpted logs (earlier).

If you prefer a brief call to walk through this, I can set up a 20-minute slot this morning.

Connor O'Brien
